scenes.visual: Title card 'One Cell, Many Jobs' over a large slipper-shaped Paramecium cartoon in moving pond water. COLOUR MAP FOR BOTH FILMS: movement BLUE, feeding GOLD, water balance TEAL, reproduction GREEN, nerve signalling VIOLET, oxygen carrying RED, shared DNA MAGENTA, tissues and organs ORANGE. Flat cartoons are labelled 'schematic'. No cell drawing is to scale.

scenes.tts: How can one cell swim, feed, control water, and reproduce without organs? In pond water, a Paramecium does all of them. Watch where each job happens.
scenes.visual: A drop of pond water expands to fill the frame. One large slipper-shaped Paramecium swims across it while four empty job rings follow: move BLUE, feed GOLD, water TEAL, reproduce GREEN. The question appears above the cell.
scenes.narration: How can one cell swim, feed, control water, and reproduce without organs? In pond water, a Paramecium does all of them. Watch where each job happens.

scenes.tts: A unicellular organism is a living thing made of one cell. It has no tissues or organs. Its whole life must work inside one boundary.
scenes.visual: The Paramecium grows to fill most of the frame. A bold outline closes around it and the label 'unicellular: one cell, one organism' settles above. Faded tissue and organ silhouettes outside the boundary slide away.
scenes.narration: A unicellular organism is a living thing made of one cell. It has no tissues or organs. Its whole life must work inside one boundary.

scenes.tts: Bacteria, many algae, and many protists are unicellular. Each is a complete organism, not one cell broken away from a larger body.
scenes.visual: The Paramecium shrinks left while a bacterium and simple alga appear beside it, each inside its own complete boundary. A torn edge labelled 'piece of a body' slides in and is crossed out.
scenes.narration: Bacteria, many algae, and many protists are unicellular. Each is a complete organism, not one cell broken away from a larger body.

scenes.tts: Short cilia cover its surface. They beat together like oars, pushing the cell through water. Movement stays a job of this same cell.
scenes.visual: BLUE cilia appear around the same large cell, then beat in a travelling wave. Water streaks slide backward while the Paramecium moves forward. The BLUE job ring locks onto the cilia.
scenes.narration: Short cilia cover its surface. They beat together like oars, pushing the cell through water. Movement stays a job of this same cell.

scenes.tts: Food such as bacteria is swept into a groove. A food vacuole closes around it and travels through the cell. Digestion also happens inside.
scenes.visual: GOLD bacteria drift toward an oral groove on the carried cell. The membrane closes around them as a GOLD food vacuole. The vacuole travels slowly across the cell while its contents break into smaller unstructured dots.
scenes.narration: Food such as bacteria is swept into a groove. A food vacuole closes around it and travels through the cell. Digestion also happens inside.

scenes.tts: These jobs do not sit in separate organs. Moving, feeding, and digesting all occur within the membrane of one working cell.
scenes.visual: The moving Paramecium, cilia, groove, and travelling food vacuole remain in one frame. Faint organ boxes try to divide them, then dissolve as the single cell boundary brightens.
scenes.narration: These jobs do not sit in separate organs. Moving, feeding, and digesting all occur within the membrane of one working cell.

scenes.tts: Pond water has fewer dissolved particles than the cell, so water keeps moving inward by osmosis. If that continued, what would the cell need to do?
scenes.visual: TEAL water arrows stream through the cell boundary. The Paramecium swells slightly, then holds. Question card: 'Water keeps entering. What must the cell do?' The contractile vacuole is not yet shown.
scenes.narration: Pond water has fewer dissolved particles than the cell, so water keeps moving inward by osmosis. If that continued, what would the cell need to do?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The water arrows continue slowly, the question remains, and a five-second ring timer fills.

scenes.tts: It must remove the extra water. Two contractile vacuoles, one toward each end, fill and squeeze water out. The cell stays intact as the cycle repeats.
scenes.visual: Two TEAL star-shaped contractile vacuoles appear inside the same cell, one toward each end. Each fills from small TEAL channels, pulses larger, touches the boundary, and empties outside. The cell returns to its earlier size; the cycle repeats once.
scenes.narration: It must remove the extra water. Two contractile vacuoles, one toward each end, fill and squeeze water out. The cell stays intact as the cycle repeats.

scenes.tts: For reproduction, the Paramecium copies what it needs and pinches into two cells. One cell has carried movement, feeding, water control, and reproduction.
scenes.visual: The four coloured job rings orbit the cell. Its contents duplicate schematically, the middle narrows, and the cell pinches into two matching Paramecia. Each daughter receives the same four rings.
scenes.narration: For reproduction, the Paramecium copies what it needs and pinches into two cells. One cell has carried movement, feeding, water control, and reproduction.

scenes.tts: Binary fission is reproduction without a partner. One cell divides into two, and each new cell must carry every life process.
scenes.visual: A GREEN label 'binary fission' follows the pinching cell. No partner enters the frame. The two daughters swim apart and each cycles through all four coloured job rings.
scenes.narration: Binary fission is reproduction without a partner. One cell divides into two, and each new cell must carry every life process.

scenes.tts: A multicellular organism can place major jobs in different cells. Those cells become specialized for particular work. Each cell's structure fits the job it does.
scenes.visual: The two Paramecium daughters swim off left, still two separate one-celled organisms. On the right a separate many-celled organism fades in, labelled 'a different organism, schematic'. The BLUE, GOLD, TEAL and GREEN job colours separate into its different cells, whose shapes begin changing around their assigned jobs.
scenes.narration: A multicellular organism can place major jobs in different cells. Those cells become specialized for particular work. Each cell's structure fits the job it does.

scenes.tts: Similar specialized cells can work as a tissue. Several tissues can build an organ. Related organs can form an organ system, all serving one organism.
scenes.visual: ORANGE specialist cells tile into a sheet labelled 'tissue'. Several differently textured tissue sheets fold into a simple heart labelled 'organ'. The heart joins schematic blood vessels labelled 'organ system', then settles inside an organism outline.
scenes.narration: Similar specialized cells can work as a tissue. Several tissues can build an organ. Related organs can form an organ system, all serving one organism.

scenes.tts: Muscle cells form muscle tissue. Several tissues form the heart. The heart works with blood vessels in the circulatory system.
scenes.visual: The hierarchy reverses slowly for a concrete example: ORANGE muscle cells tile into muscle tissue, tissues wrap into a heart, and vessels grow outward to complete the circulatory-system silhouette.
scenes.narration: Muscle cells form muscle tissue. Several tissues form the heart. The heart works with blood vessels in the circulatory system.

scenes.tts: Sharing does not erase each cell's basic work. A muscle cell still takes in food molecules, makes A T P for energy, and maintains itself. Specialized means especially fitted for a job, not limited to only one job.
scenes.visual: Zoom from the organism back into one ORANGE muscle cell. Its main shortening action grows bold, while three smaller moving icons remain inside: food molecules enter, an 'ATP' energy gauge pulses, and the membrane repairs a small gap.
scenes.narration: Sharing does not erase each cell's basic work. A muscle cell still takes in food molecules, makes ATP for energy, and maintains itself. Specialized means especially fitted for a job, not limited to only one job.
scenes.caption: Sharing does not erase each cell's basic work. A muscle cell still takes in food molecules, makes ATP for energy, and maintains itself. Specialized means especially fitted for a job, not limited to only one job.

scenes.tts: The contrast is now clear. A Paramecium keeps every life process within one cell. A many-celled organism can share major jobs across cells shaped for their work.
scenes.visual: Return to the split frame. Left: the Paramecium cycles through BLUE cilia, GOLD food, TEAL pumping, and GREEN division. Right: specialized cells pass the same coloured job tokens through tissue, organ, and organ-system silhouettes.
scenes.narration: The contrast is now clear. A Paramecium keeps every life process within one cell. A many-celled organism can share major jobs across cells shaped for their work.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'One cell can do every life job, or many cells share them.'
